newsitem.title: UK: ICI, Brit Steel seen as budget casualties.
newsitem.headline: ICI, Brit Steel seen as budget casualties.

text.p: Imperial Chemical Industries Plc and other industrial groups such as British Steel Plc and BTR Plc were the biggest fallers in the UK's FTSE 100 index on Thursday as they were seen as victims of Wednesday's budget.

Surging sterling was seen as depressing the value of their overseas earnings, while the abolition of dividend tax credits was seen as requiring them to boost the level of their payments into pensions funds.
By 0750 GMT, ICI dropped 38-1/2p or about 4.5 percent to 810p, British Steel lost 7-1/2p or 1.86 pct to 142-3/4p, and BTR fell 9p or 4.20 percent to 205-1/2p.

Analysts at BZW said nearly half of the FTSE 100 companies' pension funds could become underfunded because of the tax credit abolition, hitting earnings. Industrial companies were seen as most vulnerable.
"The companies which will be most vulnerable to the change will be those with lowly funded pension funds and where the fund is large, relative to the size of the company," BZW said in a report.

"Given that another aspect of this budget is that it looks set to give sterling another push upwards, there must be significant risk that the industrials will come under further pressure over the summer months," it said.

Sterling rose toward its five-year high against the mark on Thursday morning on expectations that interest rates will have to be boosted to cool off domestic demand in the wake of the budget, traders and analysts said.
Shares in engineering group GKN Plc dropped 38p, or 3.77 pct, to 970-1/2p.
However, other analysts said the sector's reaction was overdone.

"The pension fund situation has been overstated," said one sector analyst. "Most of the funds of these companies are heavily in surplus. There may be some adjustments to the contribution rate but it shouldn't really be that significant."
